changed: Sign in and Create an account are one form: type your email, press Continue, and a link signs you in, new or returning.
If you have a passkey, your browser offers it when you tap the email field on Sign in.
Sign in no longer has a separate passkey button.
After you ask for a sign-in link, the form steps aside and says which address the link went to.
The account page is now the account dialog: opening /account shows it over your list.
The second button of a pair, like a dialog's Cancel, is a gray pill instead of a bare word.
When a sign-in link has something to ask, it asks over the page you asked from instead of on an empty one.
The sign-in dialog is a small centered card with the Mahonia mark on top.
An expired sign-in link opens straight onto the form for a new one.
Sign in shows what went wrong in a red callout that points at the email field.
A mistyped email on Sign in shakes the sign-in card.
Dialogs close with the same quick, settled motion as menus.
Import a list is tidier: the name is a real field, Choose a file sits under the paste box, and file formats are behind a question mark.
Offline, the account button becomes a cloud with a line through it, and tapping it says your list is saved on this device.
Sign in tells you when you are offline before you press Continue.
A sign-in link opened offline waits and signs you in when you are back online.
The Gear, Packing, and Trip tabs keep their icons on a small phone.
fixed: A mistyped email on Sign in is caught before you are told to check your inbox.
Sign in says whether you are offline, asked too often, or should just try again, instead of blaming the address.
A passkey that fails to sign you in now says so.
The top bar's icons no longer bunch up unevenly beside a long status.
